\mxunit{automatismes-ch07}{Proportions and percentage change}

\begin{fluencysheet}{Tue~2~Feb.~2027}{Proportions and percentages; proportion of a proportion}
\mxfq{Warm-up · Quick}{PRO}{Calculate $\pc{15}$ of $240$.}{$\num{0,15}\times240=36$.}{}
\mxfq{Core · Method}{PRO}{$\pc{30}$ of the pupils are boarders and $\pc{40}$ of the boarders do dance. What proportion of the pupils are boarders who do dance?}{$\num{0,3}\times\num{0,4}=\num{0,12}=\pc{12}$: proportion of a proportion (we multiply).}{}
\mxfq{Core + · Problem}{PRO}{A school has $800$ pupils, of whom $\pc{55}$ are girls; $\pc{20}$ of the girls study Latin. How many girls study Latin?}{$800\times\num{0,55}=440$ girls; $440\times\num{0,20}=88$.}{}
\mxfq{Review · Quick}{QP}{$3$ exercise books cost $\num{4,50}$ €. Price of $7$ books?}{$\num{1,50}\times7=\num{10,50}$ €.}{}
\mxfq{Thread · True/false}{EQ}{True or false? Justify. The number $-2$ is a solution of the equation $3x+1=-5$.}{True. $3\times(-2)+1=-6+1=-5$.}{}
\end{fluencysheet}

\begin{fluencysheet}{Thu~4~Feb.~2027}{Absolute change, multiplier, rate of change}
\mxfq{Warm-up · Quick}{PRO}{A price goes from $80$ Ar to $92$ Ar. What is the absolute change?}{$92-80=12$ Ar.}{}
\mxfq{Core · Method}{PRO}{For the same change, give the rate of change and the multiplier.}{$t=\dfrac{12}{80}=\num{0,15}=\pc{15}$; $CM=1+t=\num{1,15}$.}{}
\mxfq{Core + · MCQ}{PRO}{A decrease of $\pc{20}$ corresponds to the multiplier:\mxchoices{$\num{0,2}$}{$-\num{0,8}$}{$\num{1,2}$}{$\num{0,8}$}}{D.\ $\num{0,8}$}{$CM=1+t=1-\num{0,20}$.}
\mxfq{Review · Quick}{STA}{Temperatures $-2,\,0,\,3,\,5,\,9$ (in °C). Mean and range?}{Mean $3$ °C; range $9-(-2)=11$ °C.}{}
\mxfq{Thread · Quick}{SOL}{Calculate the volume and the total surface area of a cube with edge $3$ cm.}{$V=3^3=27$ cm$^3$; $A=6\times3^2=54$ cm$^2$.}{}
\end{fluencysheet}

\begin{fluencysheet}{Mon~8~Feb.~2027}{Successive percentage changes}
\mxfq{Warm-up · Quick}{CAL}{Calculate $\num{1,2}\times\num{0,9}$.}{$\num{1,08}$.}{}
\mxfq{Core · Method}{PRO}{An increase of $\pc{20}$ is followed by a decrease of $\pc{10}$. What is the overall rate of change?}{$\num{1,2}\times\num{0,9}=\num{1,08}$: overall increase of $\pc{8}$.}{Rates are not added; it is the multipliers that are multiplied.}
\mxfq{Core + · True/false}{PRO}{True or false? Justify. An increase of $\pc{50}$ followed by a decrease of $\pc{50}$ returns to the initial value.}{False. $\num{1,5}\times\num{0,5}=\num{0,75}$: overall decrease of $\pc{25}$.}{}
\mxfq{Review · Quick}{SUB}{Calculate $x^2-x$ for $x=\dfrac12$.}{$-\dfrac{1}{4}$.}{}
\mxfq{Thread · Write-up}{DEM}{$ABCD$ is a parallelogram such that $AC=BD$. What type of quadrilateral is it? Justify in one sentence.}{Rectangle: a parallelogram whose diagonals have equal length is a rectangle.}{}
\end{fluencysheet}

\begin{fluencysheet}{Tue~9~Feb.~2027}{Reverse percentage change; proportion and change}
\mxfq{Warm-up · Quick}{CAL}{Calculate $\dfrac{1}{\num{1,25}}$.}{$\num{0,8}$.}{}
\mxfq{Core · Method}{PRO}{After an increase of $\pc{25}$, what decrease brings back the initial value?}{$CM_{\text{rev}}=\dfrac{1}{\num{1,25}}=\num{0,8}$: decrease of $\pc{20}$ (not $\pc{25}$).}{Pitfall: believing that an increase of $\pc{25}$ is cancelled by a decrease of $\pc{25}$.}
\mxfq{Core + · Interpret}{PRO}{Out of $250$ candidates, $150$ are successful; last year there were $200$ candidates. Calculate the proportion of successful candidates, then the rate of change of the number of candidates.}{Proportion $\dfrac{150}{250}=\pc{60}$ (part over whole); change $\dfrac{250-200}{200}=\pc{25}$ (relative change).}{}

$x$ & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline
$f(x)$ & 4 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ \hline

\mxfq{Thread · MCQ}{REP}{On the globe, two points on the same parallel have:\mxchoices{the same latitude}{the same longitude}{the same distance from Greenwich}{the same altitude}}{A.\ the same latitude}{Latitude: north/south angle from the equator; longitude: east/west angle from the Greenwich meridian.}
